references.text: Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to the Lord, just as he had done earlier in the chapter when Pharaoh asked for the plague of frogs to be removed.
Moses went out from Pharaoh and out of the city, and stretched out his hands toward the Lord - the same pattern of leaving Pharaoh to pray to God.
Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to the Lord to remove the locusts - an identical pattern of action.
Isaac prayed earnestly (עתר) to the Lord for his wife - the same Hebrew verb for earnest prayer is used.
Uses the same Hebrew verb (עתר) for prayer to God, showing earnest intercession.
Elijah is mentioned as an example of how the prayer of a righteous person has great power - Moses' intercession is a similar example of effective prayer.
A theological parallel that highlights Moses' role as an intercessor who halts God's judgment through prayer.
